topic: Ollama v0.40.11: is it worth re-pulling your models?
title: Ollama v0.40.11: re-pull your models?
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites this.
hook_text: Should you update Ollama? Nothing re-downloads.
hook_candidates: Should you update Ollama? Nothing re-downloads.
Three moves and Ollama's updated tonight.
Update pings Ollama. Your models stay put.
One hundred thirteen megabytes buys Ollama speech.
Ollama's update never touches your pulled models.
You run Ollama. The update ping landed. Relax.

v0.40.11 ships speech. Your disk stays calm.
narration_full: Should you update Ollama tonight? Nothing re-downloads. Your models stay safe on disk. Updates swap the app, nothing else. One click. Your pulls sit in a folder it never touches. New player, same songs. What's new: speech on macOS, replies read aloud. That's phonon, a speech model. It turns text into audio, and the whole feature is a hundred and thirteen megabytes on disk. Meet d3, a decision model that scores options instead of chatting. The smallest is two billion parameters. It pulls about three gigabytes on disk. The catch: zero point forty point two rewrote old models once, backups kept. Updates never re-pull. A downgrade can. Update always, re-pull never, and pull new only when a feature names a model.

analogy.vehicle: Updating the music player app on your phone
analogy.mapping: Updating Ollama swaps the player app; your pulled models are the songs already on storage; you only download again when you want a new album, which is phonon or d3.
analogy.limit: Songs are inert but models are format-coupled to the engine: v0.40.2 rewrote old models in the background once, backup kept, so the analogy breaks at any future format swap.

notes_for_review: Consequence ('the update leaves them alone') is spoken at about second 3, before any feature, per the news-react-so-what order. Spoken numbers spent: a hundred and thirteen megabytes (phonon pull), two billion parameters (smallest d3), about three gigabytes (d3 pull), plus the version string zero point forty point two spoken once; v0.40.11 is kept off-screen because unspoken numbers cannot render. The music-player analogy lands in s02 and its stated limit becomes the catch in s05. At about 2.7 words per second this runs near 40 s, inside the 28-60 band; tighten inter-scene pauses to approach 35.
